plate_findings.evidence: transection of adult worm surrounded by granuloma

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E stained section showing a transected adult Loa loa worm surrounded by granulomatous inflammation, a classic histologic manifestation of loiasis. B: High magnification H&E showing the worm section within a granuloma composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes, and plasma cells. C: Immunohistochemistry demonstrating numerous CD4 lymphocytes infiltrating the granuloma around the worm section. D: Immunohistochemistry showing fewer CD8 lymphocytes in the granulomatous reaction. E: Immunohistochemistry showing sparse CD19 B-cell infiltration around the worm. F: Immunohistochemistry showing few CD56 natural killer cells in the granulomatous tissue.
panels.attribution_text: Li et al. Clinical and epidemiological features of imported loiasis in Beijing: a report from patients returned from Africa.. BMC infectious diseases 2024. doi:10.1186/s12879-024-09620-6. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathologic features and immunohistochemistry of skin module infected with L. loa adult worm. Hematoxylin-eosin stained section of skin nodule tissue under microscope exhibited a transection of adult worm (A, arrows, 10 × magnification) surrounded by the granuloma, lymphocytes, plasma cells and eosinophils (B, 100 × magnification). There are many CD4 lymphocyte filtrated around the worm (C, 100 × magnification), less CD8 (D, 100 × magnification) and few CD 19 (E, 100 × magnification) and CD 56 positive cells in the granuloma (F, 100 × magnification)
in_text_mentions: Biopsy was performed on a patient with obvious skin module located on the right forearm. The histological examination on the biopsy section showed a transection of an adult worm surrounded by the granuloma and inflammatory cells infiltrated including many eosinophils (Fig. 3A and B). The immunohistochemistry staining showed the significant filtration of CD4 lymphocytes followed by the CD8 cells in the granuloma surrounding the parasite section. There were few CD19 and CD56 cells filtration (Fig. 3 C-F).

plate_findings.evidence: Typical Calabar swellings seen during the study of hands (A-E) and face (F)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Clinical photograph of the palms showing typical Calabar swellings, a characteristic transient angioedema manifestation of loiasis. B: Clinical photograph of the dorsum of the hands showing typical Calabar swellings, a characteristic manifestation of loiasis. C: Clinical photograph of the hands showing typical Calabar swellings, a characteristic manifestation of loiasis. D: Clinical photograph of the palms showing typical Calabar swellings, a characteristic manifestation of loiasis. E: Clinical photograph of the dorsum of the hands showing typical Calabar swellings, a characteristic manifestation of loiasis. F: Clinical photograph of the periorbital face showing a typical Calabar swelling, a characteristic manifestation of loiasis. G: Ultrasound image of the orbital Calabar swelling shown in panel F, demonstrating associated edema consistent with the transient angioedema of loiasis.
panels.attribution_text: Veletzky et al. Understanding Calabar swellings: Assessing subcutaneous loiasis using ultrasound.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases 2026. doi:10.1371/journal.pntd.0014240. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: “Typical” Calabar swellings seen during the study of hands (A-E) and face (F) as well as an ultrasound image (G: white arrow indicating the bone, black bracket indicating the edema) of the orbital swelling depicted in (F). Pictures A to F were taken by LV.
in_text_mentions: Overall, 22 individuals had visible swellings identified by the fieldworker and were further examined clinically and by ultrasound. Details on the study population are shown in Table 1, and Fig 1 provides pictures of “typical CS” observed during the study. A more comprehensive overview, including detailed descriptions of the swellings is provided in S1 Table.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (2a, 2b, 2c). 2a: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) horizontal cross-section of a pediatric patient's right eye showing hyperreflective areas in the subconjunctival space corresponding to a Loa loa larva, a classic manifestation of loiasis. 2b: AS-OCT vertical cross-section of the same pediatric patient's right eye confirming the presence of a Loa loa larva in the subconjunctival space, consistent with loiasis. 2c: Infrared image of a pediatric patient's right eye directly visualizing a Loa loa larva in the subconjunctival space, a classic clinical manifestation of loiasis.
panels.attribution_text: Placinta et al. Ocular loiasis affecting a child and its assessment by Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography.. Romanian journal of ophthalmology 2019. doi:10.22336/rjo.2019.28. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: CASIA AS-OCT image composition of right eye. a. Horizontal cross-section (at the level of yellow line in Fig. 2c) evidencing hyperreflective areas surrounded by larger hyporeflective areas in the subconjunctival space, corresponding with the Loa loa larva; b. Vertical cross-section (perpendicular to yellow cross-section line in Fig. 2c) showing hyperreflective areas surrounded by larger hyporeflective areas in the subconjunctival space corresponding with the Loa loa larva. c. Super temporal quadrant infrared image showing Loa loa larva in the subconjunctival space
in_text_mentions: That same evening, she turned back to the emergency room complaining of tingling and the presence of the worm in her right eye. Slit lamp examination confirmed the presence of the worm under the medial bulbar conjunctiva. Again, 10% phenylephrine, 1% tropicamide, 0,1% tetracaine and 0,4% oxybuprocaine were instilled in an attempt of numbing the conjunctiva and paralyzing the worm for eventual surgical extraction. While waiting for proper numbing, anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) was performed to document the larva (Fig. 2,3).

b. Vertical cross-section (perpendicular to yellow cross-section line in Fig. 2c) showing hyperreflective areas surrounded by larger hyporeflective areas in the subconjunctival space corresponding with the Loa loa larva.

A la lampe a fente on notait à l’œil droit une hyperhémie conjonctivale diffuse, on observait sous la conjonctive bulbaire un cordon blanc tortueux ondulant (Figure 1) et mobile. Le reste de l’examen était sans particularité. Devant ce tableau clinique une extraction chirurgicale non traumatique du ver était réalisée (Figure 2, Figure 3). Il s’agissait d’un ver vivant et d’environ 4cm de long translucide mobile (Figure 4) recueillie et adressé au laboratoire pour l’analyse où la Loa loa a été confirmée. Le patient a été mis systématiquement sous traite

findings.label: Subconjunctival Loa loa worm
findings.evidence: Caption states 'Subconjunctival Loa loa Worm Observed in Patient's Left Eye'

panels.rationale: Patient-provided clinical photograph demonstrating a subconjunctival Loa loa worm in the left eye, a classic manifestation of loiasis. The image shows a thin, motile worm crossing the conjunctiva with associated erythema of the surrounding tissue.
panels.attribution_text: Root et al. Delayed-Onset Loiasis: A Case of Loa loa Infection Diagnosed Six Years Post-exposure.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.86135. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Subconjunctival Loa loa Worm Observed in Patient's Left Eye
in_text_mentions: Upon physical examination of the left eye, the conjunctiva was erythemic but without periorbital swelling or lid edema. All extraocular muscles were intact, and pupils were equal and reactive to light bilaterally. Fundoscopic exam was unremarkable, with no evidence of retinal or optic disc involvement. There was no evidence of a worm in her sclera; however, a small worm-like organism was identified actively moving over the patient’s upper eyelid. The right eye was unremarkable. The patient shared images from her personal phone revealing a subconjunctival parasite in her left eye (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: This is a clear real human patient clinical color photograph showing a classic, pathognomonic manifestation of loiasis (subconjunctival Loa loa larva) in the right eye, as explicitly confirmed by the figure caption and accompanying in-text ophthalmic examination findings. No excluded features (diagrams, other disease, control images, etc.) are present.
panels.attribution_text: Placinta et al. Ocular loiasis affecting a child and its assessment by Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography.. Romanian journal of ophthalmology 2019. doi:10.22336/rjo.2019.28. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Color photography of patient’s right eye. Loa loa larva can be observed at the inferior subconjunctival space
in_text_mentions: Visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes. On slit lamp examination, a large, translucent, coiled, slowly moving worm was observed underneath the inferior bulbar conjunctiva on the patient’s right eye (Fig. 1). No other pathological findings were observed on anterior and posterior pole examination.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph showing urticarial and papular skin lesions on the thigh of a patient with loiasis. B: Clinical photograph showing urticarial skin lesion behind the ear of a patient with loiasis.

panels.figure_caption: Cutaneous manifestations of Loa loa (African eye worm) infection in a US traveler who returned from a 6-month stay on Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea, 2016. Urticarial lesions on the left thigh showing a coincident papular eruption (A) and behind the left ear (B).
